organizations.What they build: Korean automotive group and Robotics LAB. Builds MobED, a modular wheeled robot that keeps its payload level on uneven ground, offered as Basic and autonomous Pro configurations. Its own factories are a potential customer for robotics; US subsidiary Boston Dynamics is outside this organization slice.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: Robotics LAB enquiry or an introduction through KAR/ROBOTWORLD; no personal connection verified.
organizations._relationship_reason: A remote talk on navigation, mobility platforms, or factory validation is plausible. A free mobile robot or direct corporate sponsorship is not evidenced; first show a reproducible navigation demo.

organizations.What they build: Develops Ballie, a wheeled home companion combining cameras, conversational AI, and connected-home control. Announced an increase to 35% of Rainbow Robotics in December 2024 and plans to combine AI with Rainbow hardware for humanoids and manufacturing/logistics automation. Ballie commercial availability is unknown; an announced launch target is not proof of shipment.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: Samsung robotics research outreach or a KAR introduction. No student partnership verified.
organizations._relationship_reason: A technical speaker on home-robot perception is a more realistic first request than funding or prototype access. Rainbow is separately represented as the Korean hardware builder.

organizations.What they build: Presented CLOiD, a wheeled two-arm home robot, at CES 2026 and introduced AXIUM robot actuators. CLOiD combines a vision-language model (interprets images and instructions) with a vision-language-action model (turns those inputs into actions); individual model names and open weights are unknown. The opened source demonstrates a product direction, not verified retail availability.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: LG robotics or university-relations enquiry, with KAR as a possible introduction.
organizations._relationship_reason: A remote speaker on household manipulation and appliance integration is plausible after a student demo. No open robot API, free hardware, or student sponsorship scheme was established.

organizations.What they build: Makes collaborative robot arms and automation solutions. P3020 is a five-axis palletizing arm that moves boxes onto pallets, with 30 kg payload and 2,030 mm reach. Its public doosan-robot2 ROS 2 packages expose robot control and simulation integration; open software does not mean open robot hardware.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: sales.robotics@doosan.com or the official ROS 2 repository issue tracker for a specific technical question.
organizations._relationship_reason: Begin with a ROS 2 simulation example or integration contribution and ask for a control/automation speaker. A partner lab or distributor demonstration is more plausible than purchasing a heavy industrial cell.

organizations.What they build: KAIST spin-out building robot platforms. RB-Y1 combines two seven-joint arms with a wheeled base for manipulation, teleoperation, and whole-body-control research. Provides Python/C++ SDK and simulation assets. Samsung announced its 35% stake and subsidiary consolidation in December 2024; this does not make the hardware open source.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: official RB-Y1 support channel or an SDK issue/discussion, backed by a concrete reproducible demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: Contribute a simulation or teleoperation example and seek researcher feedback or a remote talk. Hardware access would require an institutional partner; no loan or student discount was verified.

organizations.What they build: Builds DYNAMIXEL smart actuators and open research platforms: TurtleBot3, OMX entry-level arms, OMY manipulators, AI Worker mobile manipulators, and AI Sapiens humanoids. Physical AI Tools links ROS 2 robot control to LeRobot demonstration datasets and policy training. This is the strongest direct software bridge to 42AI in the shortlist; actual landed hardware prices remain unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown personal connection; public route: ROBOTIS Discourse forum and a useful Physical AI Tools GitHub issue/PR, then its global contact form.
organizations._relationship_reason: 42AI can publish a small ROS 2/LeRobot data-collection contribution without first buying a humanoid. After that, ask for a mentor and educational pricing or a loan of an OMX/TurtleBot kit; neither discount nor loan is confirmed.

organizations.What they build: Korean wearable/humanoid startup. Sells WIM walking-assistance devices and develops ALLEX upper-body humanoid hardware for compliant, dexterous manipulation. Announced KRW 95 billion Series B in May 2026. Its BSD-licensed ALLEX simulation model is public; the repository calls physical hardware research-prototype v2 with limited research-edition access planned later in 2026, not a mass-market robot.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: official contact form, ALLEX model repository, or an introduction via investor FuturePlay.
organizations._relationship_reason: A simulation-only manipulation benchmark or model issue report fits the team skill set. Ask for sim-to-real mentoring after shipping results; prototype access and investment in a student association are not assumed.

organizations.What they build: NAVER research organization building ARC cloud robotics: cloud-side robot management, localization, and a web operating layer. Builds and tests Rookie delivery robots and AMBIDEX dual-arm manipulation, connecting a heterogeneous robot fleet in NAVER 1784. An April 2025 official account reports about 100 robots and over 60,000 deliveries; these are company-reported historical figures.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: NAVER LABS research enquiry or public conference speakers; no existing 42AI connection verified.
organizations._relationship_reason: A remote talk on fleet orchestration, digital twins, and deployment metrics is realistic. Propose an open miniature delivery-fleet demo; access to NAVER 1784, proprietary cloud services, or compute is unconfirmed.

organizations.What they build: University with multiple robotics groups. Its DRCD Lab builds HOUND quadrupeds with custom drivetrains and learned locomotion; HOUND 1 used a reinforcement-learning controller for its 2023 speed demonstration. HOUND 2 is a newer lab platform, but its official page gives conflicting mass figures. This row represents the university; the lab is a contact route, not a duplicate organization.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: DRCD lab contact at its official KAIST site, or a specific corresponding author with a reproducible research question.
organizations._relationship_reason: Seek a graduate-student talk or paper-reproduction feedback rather than access to a custom quadruped. A software-only locomotion replication is feasible in 4-6 months; building HOUND mechanics is not.

organizations.Organization: Korea Institute of Robotics & Technology Convergence (KIRO)
organizations.What they build: Public applied-robotics institute linking university research to industrial deployment. Works on underwater, disaster-response, in-pipe/construction, agricultural and manufacturing robotics; its marine division documents the P-SURO underwater robot family. Operates RoTIC industrial-robot education facilities. Older marine pages establish platforms, not a 2026 commercial release.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: KIRO international contact or RoTIC education enquiry. No Paris exchange or free training eligibility verified.
organizations._relationship_reason: A remote seminar on testing robots in real environments or an exchange of educational material is plausible. In-person industrial training would require travel, fees, and eligibility checks; do not assume hardware access.

organizations.Organization: Korea Association of AI Robot Industry (KAR)
organizations.What they build: Industry association connecting Korean government, companies, and academia. Coordinates industry networking and is a ROBOTWORLD organizer; does not itself have a verified named robot or AI model. The English home page now uses Korea Association of AI Robot Industry, while the page title retains the earlier Korea Association of Robot Industry wording.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: KAR international-relations enquiry or ROBOTWORLD secretariat (info@robotworld.or.kr). No warm introduction exists in the evidence.
organizations._relationship_reason: Ask for introductions to ROS/robot-learning educators and Korean firms with European outreach. A student demo and concrete speaker request are a reasonable basis; sponsorship is not established.

organizations.What they build: Korean robotics trade exhibition covering manufacturers, service robots, components, software, and integration. The official 2026 dates are November 4-7 at KINTEX, so that edition has already ended as of this research on November 13. Organizer-page participation counts conflict and are not treated as verified 2026 totals. No named robot or AI model is built by the event.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: info@robotworld.or.kr for post-event exhibitor introductions or a future student delegation. Next edition dates unknown.
organizations._relationship_reason: Use exhibitor connections for a remote Korean-robotics speaker series now; consider a future visit only if travel funding exists. No student showcase place, hackathon, or invitation is confirmed.

organizations.What they build: Deep-tech venture investor providing early-stage funding and company-building support. Its official portfolio includes WIRobotics; WIRobotics also names FuturePlay among its May 2026 Series B investors. It invests in robotics companies rather than building or operating a verified named robot itself. The investor own financing stage is unknown, so Size / stage is left null.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: communication@futureplay.co with a specific portfolio-company introduction or deep-tech speaker request.
organizations._relationship_reason: A venture/technical speaker or portfolio introduction is realistic; an equity investor is not a default sponsor of a French student association. A mature student spin-out could later become an investment conversation.

organizations.What they build: Korean online robotics community with public ROS teaching repositories and the iTurtle miniature robot project, explicitly based on TurtleBot3. The cited iTurtle repository documents the Pangyo chapter and links the Naver community. Evidence for these projects is historical; community activity and maintainership in 2026 are unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; public route: linked OROCA Naver cafe or GitHub issues, first checking whether maintainers are active and whether English outreach is welcome.
organizations._relationship_reason: Offer a bilingual tutorial or a small reproducible ROS example, then explore a remote student demo exchange. Do not plan a scheduled event or count on current maintainers until they respond.

organizations.What they build: Seoul startup rooted in Seoul National University AI research. Co-developed CLIP-RT, a one-billion-parameter vision-language-action model (camera images and instructions to robot motions), with public code and checkpoints. In 2026 presented HABILIS Brain 0 and a stack for data, training, deployment, and robot operations. Funding stage is unknown; an investment target is not a completed round.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown personal connection; public route: partnerships@tommoro.ai or the CLIP-RT repository with a reproducible evaluation question.
organizations.Sources: https://tommoro.ai/; https://tommoro.ai/about; https://tommoro.ai/contact; https://www.snu.ac.kr/snunow/press?bbsidx=154981&md=v; https://clip-rt.github.io/; https://github.com/clip-rt/clip-rt; https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25558
organizations._relationship_reason: The public CLIP-RT code is a practical software contribution and paper-reproduction route for 42AI. Ask for researcher feedback or a remote speaker after sharing benchmark results; HABILIS commercial access and sponsorship are not established.

robots_models.Name: MobED
robots_models.Price / access: Price unknown; commercial platform enquiry. Source announced mass production for H1 2026; actual student access unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Modular wheeled platform with active posture/height control and mounting rails. Basic is a research base; Pro adds LiDAR-camera fusion and autonomous/follow-me modes. Production-ready version unveiled December 2025.
robots_models.Why it matters: A useful reference for mobility on uneven terrain; too much custom mechanical work to reproduce as a first student build.

robots_models.Name: Ballie
robots_models.Price / access: Price and actual commercial availability unknown; April 2025 source announced a summer 2025 launch target, not delivery evidence.
robots_models.Key specs: Mobile home companion with camera/sensors and connected-home control; April 2025 announcement pairs Google Cloud Gemini with proprietary Samsung language models. Version and model weights unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Illustrates conversational HRI and service orchestration; no confirmed student developer platform.

robots_models.Name: LG CLOiD
robots_models.Price / access: CES 2026 demonstration; retail price, shipping, and research access unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Head, tilting torso, two articulated arms and autonomous wheeled base; seven joints per arm and five independently actuated fingers per hand. Company describes VLM/VLA household skills and ThinQ integration.
robots_models.Why it matters: Relevant household-manipulation reference; a demo announcement does not establish affordable or open hardware.

robots_models.Name: P3020
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial quote; total cost with gripper, guarding, and integration unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Five-axis palletizing collaborative arm; 30 kg payload, 2,030 mm reach, ±0.1 mm repeatability. First announced in May 2024.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows industrial demand for reliable handling; access through a partner cell is more realistic than a student purchase.

robots_models.Name: doosan-robot2
robots_models.Price / access: Public repository; root LICENSE BSD-3-Clause. Review bundled assets and emulator terms separately.
robots_models.Key specs: Official ROS 2 robot-control packages, descriptions and simulation/emulation integration. Opened default branch targets Humble. Root LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause, although README includes an Apache badge; use file-level licenses.
robots_models.Why it matters: Students can study industrial arm integration in software before requesting a physical demonstration.

robots_models.Name: RB-Y1
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial/research quote; price unknown. SDK is open; complete hardware is not established as open source.
robots_models.Key specs: Wheeled dual-arm research platform; each arm has seven joints and 3 kg payload. Open SDK supports teleoperation, manipulation learning, and whole-body control. Total joint count varies by configuration and conflicts within the current product page; not consolidated here.
robots_models.Why it matters: A strong higher-cost target for bimanual policy transfer after an inexpensive arm demo.

robots_models.Name: RB-Y1 SDK
robots_models.Price / access: Free Apache-2.0 SDK; physical robot separately purchased or accessed through a research partner.
robots_models.Key specs: Official Python/C++ control API and research examples for RB-Y1. Developer manual states Apache-2.0 licensing and describes model assets and real-time streaming.
robots_models.Why it matters: A software contribution or simulated manipulation example is a credible first contact with Rainbow researchers.

robots_models.Name: TurtleBot3
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial kit; current EUR price, shipping and taxes unknown. Documentation and simulation are publicly accessible.
robots_models.Key specs: Modular education/research robot family developed by ROBOTIS in 2017. ROS documentation covers current ROS 2 support and Raspberry Pi 4 configurations; exact sensors/payload depend on variant.
robots_models.Why it matters: An accessible reference for navigation and ROS learning, though less direct than an arm for manipulation projects.

robots_models.Name: OMX
robots_models.Price / access: Price unknown; commercial kit/parts. Public software, simulation resources, and printable designs available; confirm individual licenses before redistribution.
robots_models.Key specs: OMX-F follower plus OMX-L leader: each has five arm joints plus gripper; DYNAMIXEL-X actuators. Follower reach 400 mm, mass 560 g; payload 100 g at full reach or 250 g at normal reach. ROS 2/LeRobot workflow; drawings and printable parts published.
robots_models.Why it matters: Best direct hardware candidate to compare against the existing SO-101 approach before choosing a supplier.

robots_models.Name: OMY
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial quote; current price unknown. Public ROS 2 packages, simulation resources, and drawings; individual asset licenses need checking.
robots_models.Key specs: Six-joint DYNAMIXEL-Y manipulator family plus gripper, with leader/follower configurations, ROS 2 and human-demonstration learning support. Do not confuse its joint count with the seven-joint AI Worker arms.
robots_models.Why it matters: Intermediate platform for a later manipulation upgrade, rather than a required first purchase.

robots_models.Name: AI Worker
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial quote; price unknown. Source code, simulation and design resources published.
robots_models.Key specs: Semi-humanoid dual-arm research family with fixed/mobile variants, ROS 2 and Physical AI Tools. May 2025 official demo collected teleoperation data and trained an ACT imitation-learning policy. Specifications vary by model.
robots_models.Why it matters: Direct example of a ROS 2 to LeRobot learning pipeline; useful even when students cannot obtain the larger robot.

robots_models.Name: AI Sapiens
robots_models.Price / access: Price and purchase availability unknown; public platform/learning resources. Exact release year unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: 23-DOF humanoid platform driven by DYNAMIXEL-Q quasi-direct-drive actuators; company describes IL/RL policies deployed to physical hardware. Official product page labels its platform and repositories open source.
robots_models.Why it matters: A later locomotion/manipulation research reference; physical balance and custom hardware increase difficulty substantially.

robots_models.Name: Physical AI Tools
robots_models.Price / access: Free Apache-2.0 source; robot hardware and external compute are separate costs.
robots_models.Key specs: Official ROS 2/LeRobot development interface for demonstration data, policy workflows, and ROBOTIS platform integrations. Apache-2.0 repository created in April 2025.
robots_models.Why it matters: Highest-value software contribution target: test a narrow data-collection or dataset interoperability task and publish a reusable example.

robots_models.Name: WIM
robots_models.Price / access: Sold commercially; model-specific price and European support terms unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Commercial walking-assistance wearable family. May 2026 company-hosted funding news reports more than 3,000 cumulative unit sales and a WIM Premium subscription; no clinical efficacy claim is inferred.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows wearable-robot demand and a route to mentoring on human interaction; mechanically and clinically harder than a tabletop manipulation demo.

robots_models.Name: ALLEX
robots_models.Price / access: Research prototype; limited research edition planned later in 2026 per repository, delivery unconfirmed. Price unknown; open simulation is a separate row.
robots_models.Key specs: Upper-body dexterous humanoid first unveiled August 2025. Current public simulation describes 48 actuated DOF: two 7-DOF arms, two 15-DOF hands, two waist joints, two neck joints. Hardware is research-prototype v2; capabilities are company-reported.
robots_models.Why it matters: A credible dexterous-manipulation research target after simulation; do not budget for readily available complete hardware.

robots_models.Name: ALLEX Simulation Model
robots_models.Price / access: Free BSD-3-Clause repository; MuJoCo, ROS, or Isaac/OpenUSD tooling needed separately.
robots_models.Key specs: BSD-3-Clause multi-format robot assets: MJCF, URDF, USD and meshes, version v0.2.0 pre-release. Represents 48 actuated DOF and 12 passive couplings; URDF is kinematic and USD is experimental. Research model, not manufacturing CAD.
robots_models.Why it matters: Best zero-hardware Korean humanoid entry point: reproduce a small simulation benchmark and report model discrepancies before attempting sim-to-real.

robots_models.Name: ARC
robots_models.Price / access: Proprietary/partner system; public price, open weights, and student API access unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Cloud robotics system: ARC brain manages and controls robots; ARC eye provides spatial/localization services; ARC mind is a web-based operating system. Connects heterogeneous robots and building infrastructure over a cloud/5G architecture.
robots_models.Why it matters: A real-deployment architecture to study for fleet orchestration; access should not be assumed from public descriptions.

robots_models.Name: Rookie 2
robots_models.Price / access: Internal/partner deployment; sale price and external developer access unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Indoor service/delivery robot named among NAVER in-house ARC platforms. NAVER 1784 deployment integrates robots with elevators and cloud-side control; published fleet totals are not a Rookie 2 model count.
robots_models.Why it matters: Illustrates the operational work beyond navigation: dispatch, building integration, and delivery reliability.

robots_models.Name: AMBIDEX
robots_models.Price / access: Research platform; external access and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Dual-arm research robot named among NAVER in-house ARC platforms. Public overview establishes bimanual manipulation and cloud integration; payload, price and current robot version unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: A Korean reference for compliant two-arm manipulation; use as a research comparison rather than presumed available lab equipment.

robots_models.Name: KAIST HOUND 1
robots_models.Price / access: Custom university research hardware; price, reproducible bill of materials and public policy checkpoint unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: DRCD Lab custom quadruped, mass 45 kg. Official page reports 100 m in 19.87 s in October 2023 using a single reinforcement-learning controller, plus 22-degree slopes and 35 cm obstacles. Hardware design paper published at ICRA 2022.
robots_models.Why it matters: A strong locomotion/control reference, with a mechanical burden beyond a first software-heavy student project.

robots_models.Name: KAIST HOUND 2
robots_models.Price / access: Custom university platform; price and outside hardware access unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Newer DRCD Lab high-speed quadruped with in-house motors, drives, gears, and communications. Official prose says 53 kg while its table says 52 kg; exact mass and speed unverified. Release year unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows why impressive locomotion often needs specialized hardware; useful for a paper discussion, not a low-cost purchase recommendation.

robots_models.Name: P-SURO II
Built by: Korea Institute of Robotics & Technology Convergence (KIRO)
robots_models.Price / access: Historical applied-research platform; current access, sale status and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Hybrid remotely operated/autonomous underwater research vehicle. KIRO marine page identifies P-SURO II and a July 2010-March 2015 development period. No 2026 sale or deployment claim is inferred; schema lacks an underwater form-factor option.
robots_models.Why it matters: Illustrates navigation and sensing beyond land robots, but waterproofing and underwater mechanics make it a poor first 42AI build.

robots_models.Name: iTurtle
robots_models.Price / access: Public Apache-2.0 repository; parts cost and current kit availability unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Pangyo chapter community mini-project based on TurtleBot3, with public Python/C++/CMake code. Historical repository created in 2019; current maintenance and build readiness unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: A concrete bilingual/community documentation contribution is possible after checking whether the project still builds and maintainers respond.

robots_models.Name: ACT (Action Chunking with Transformers)
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Tony Z. Zhao and coauthors, ALOHA research project (outside the Korean organization slice)
robots_models.Price / access: Public paper, linked code and simulation; robot data and training compute required. Check code license for the chosen implementation.
robots_models.Key specs: Imitation-learning policy predicts chunks of future joint actions from images and robot observations. ROBOTIS explicitly identifies ACT as its AI Worker policy in May 2025; this is not a ROBOTIS-authored foundation model.
robots_models.Why it matters: A named model with verified use by a Korean organization. Lets students compare a concrete demonstrated policy before assuming a VLA is needed.

robots_models.Name: CLIP-RT
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): Co-builder: Seoul National University AI Institute (not separately mapped)
robots_models.Price / access: Public MIT-licensed code and linked pretrained checkpoints; confirm dataset/checkpoint terms separately. Training or fine-tuning requires compute and task data.
robots_models.Key specs: One-billion-parameter VLA uses contrastive imitation learning and language-based motion primitives. RSS 2025 project. Current project/repository reports 93.1% LIBERO success and 163 Hz throughput, while May 2025 SNU release says 92.8%; these are source-specific research results, not independently reproduced.
robots_models.Why it matters: A Korean-developed, publicly reproducible alternative for testing whether language-guided data collection helps beginners. Initial preprint predates the 2025 code/conference release, so exact first release year is not consolidated.

robots_models.Name: HABILIS Brain 0
robots_models.Price / access: Public 2026 preprint and company description; reusable model weights, code license, API access and commercial price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Geometry-Change VLA predicts visual geometry changes to guide continuous robot actions; a residual recovery policy corrects actions using closed-loop feedback. Paper reports LIBERO success of 95.20% for GC-VLA and 99.55% with recovery; not independently reproduced or proof of general deployment reliability.
robots_models.Why it matters: Connects Korean robot-learning research to manufacturing/logistics offerings; compare open CLIP-RT first and treat HABILIS access as unconfirmed.

robots_models.Name: HABILIS Console
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial/partner enquiry; source license, public API, student access and price unknown.
robots_models.Key specs: Company-described software for collecting robot data and managing training, inference, deployment, models, and robot operations. Part of the HABILIS stack; version and deployment requirements unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Relevant to the full student workflow from demonstration datasets to repeated demos; public marketing is not proof of a free service.

summary: Who leads: Hyundai, Samsung/Rainbow, LG, Doosan and ROBOTIS anchor Korean hardware; NAVER LABS contributes deployed cloud robotics, KAIST research, and Tommoro Korean VLA models.
Where money is: conglomerate-backed humanoids, actuators and industrial automation, plus venture-backed physical AI; WIRobotics announced a KRW 95 billion Series B in May 2026.
Where demand is: factory handling and palletizing, building logistics, and walking assistance already have concrete products or deployments; home manipulation remains less accessible to students.
Best technical wedge to test: contribute a ROS 2/LeRobot workflow using ROBOTIS tools or benchmark the BSD-licensed ALLEX simulation before paying for complex hardware.

Best entry point for 42AI: publish a small reproducible demo, approach ROBOTIS maintainers and Korean researchers for remote mentoring, then use KAR/FuturePlay introductions; ROBOTWORLD 2026 has ended.
